title: `migrate` from gcs backend is broken (context canceled / timeout)
body: I'm trying to migrate Vault storage from GCS to another backend, initially Raft and also file, but the migration eventually fails with `context canceled`. The first run consistently fails after roughly 37.5k copied items. If I restart with `-start` at the last copied item, it remains at `[DEBUG] creating client` for about 4m20s and then reports `failed to scan for children: failed to read object: context canceled`. Emptying the destination directory does not change the result. The VM has enough CPU, RAM, and disk and is in the same region as the GCS bucket. This is blocking our production system. I'm using Vault CLI v1.41.1 on Debian 12.

symptoms_visible: My GCS migration to Raft or file consistently stops with `context canceled`, with the first run reaching about 37.5k items.
When I resume with `-start`, it stays at `[DEBUG] creating client` for about 4m20s and then reports `failed to scan for children: failed to read object: context canceled`.
The same thing happens even after I empty the file destination.
N0.label: N0 opaque migration cancellation reported

symptoms_visible: My instrumented runs cancel at roughly 16,483 to 16,490 scanned items.
For the last prefix, the cancellation follows the first object fetch within milliseconds rather than after a long GCS request.
Changing `max-parallel` or creating a new GCS storage client for each `List` call does not change the observed cancellation point.
N1.label: N1 source-list timing instrumented

symptoms_visible: When I comment out the destination `Put` in a diagnostic build, the scan completes instead of ending with `context canceled`.
N2.label: N2 destination write isolated

symptoms_visible: With extra logging around the destination write, the file migration prints `file name too long` for a generated temporary path.
The Raft migration prints `put failed due to value being too large; got 1742831 bytes, max: 1048576 bytes` for one entry.
N3.label: N3 hidden destination errors surfaced

symptoms_visible: I found and deleted the oversized secret, and the migration issue is resolved.
N_terminal.label: terminal oversized secret removed

question_patterns: Can you add diagnostic logging around `dfsScan` and report the exact prefix being processed when the error occurs?
Could you build a diagnostic copy that logs the key passed to the storage list operation when migration cancels?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I added logging around `dfsScan` and the GCS `List` iterator. The failing prefix is a deeply nested `logical/.../metadata/.../` path, but that prefix contains only one object. The log reaches `Fetching next object` and then reports the cancellation only milliseconds later. Across repeated runs I get about 16,483 to 16,490 scanned items; changing `max-parallel` or creating a fresh storage client for every `List` does not change it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing prefix contains several million immediate children, and the GCS list request remains pending until its request deadline expires.
The same one-object prefix is logged, but repeated runs cancel a few hundred items apart instead of within a range of about ten.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c1-c9: participant1 requested the failing list path; the reporter built instrumented copies and supplied raw prefixes, timestamps, item counts, and configuration-variation results. These were diagnostic builds, not retained production changes.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily skip the destination write in a diagnostic build and report whether traversal still cancels?
Could you isolate the source scan from the destination operation and tell me whether a read-only traversal completes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I commented out the `Put` call in `operator_migrate.go` and ran it again. With the write skipped, it worked and the scan completed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It still cancels at the same point even with every destination `Put` skipped.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c10: skipping `Put` was a handler-relevant isolation measurement performed in a diagnostic build. Its raw outcome localizes the failing phase without itself changing the retained migration system.

question_patterns: Can you log the error returned directly by the destination write and paste the exact output for the file destination?
What error does the underlying file backend return before the migrate command reports cancellation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After logging the error directly around `to.Put`, the file destination reports `open data2/logical/.../_11uciVQ7...temp: file name too long`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The destination write succeeds, and the only error still comes directly from the GCS read operation.

question_patterns: Please capture the exact underlying destination-write error when using Raft.
What does direct logging around the Raft `Put` call print for the entry that stops migration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: For Raft, my added write log says: `put failed due to value being too large; got 1742831 bytes, max: 1048576 bytes`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Raft accepts the 1,742,831-byte entry and migration later fails during another GCS list call.
Raft rejects a slightly different entry size, but it is still larger than the logged 1,048,576-byte maximum.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c11-c12 and c19: extra logging around the existing `Put` call exposed the raw backend errors. The file and Raft outputs describe separate destination constraints encountered while migrating the same GCS data; this graph follows the Raft resolution.

solution.intent: Treat the opaque cancellation as a masked destination-write failure, locate the oversized KVv2 entry that exceeds the Raft destination limit, remove it if it is no longer needed, and rerun the migration to verify completion.
solution.concrete_example: The source GCS listing is not timing out: migration completes its traversal when `Put` is skipped, and direct Raft logging rejects a 1,742,831-byte value against a 1,048,576-byte maximum. Vault migration does not split or repack entries for a destination with a smaller limit. Find the corresponding oversized KVv2 secret/version, delete it if appropriate, then rerun the migration and confirm that it completes. The reporter chose this route rather than changing the default Raft limit.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw timing, isolation, and backend-error output. Concluding that the generic `context canceled` message masks a destination `Put` failure—and that GCS traversal is not the root cause—is the engineer-side inference supported by those measurements.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c13-c17: participant1 explained that migration cannot realistically repack data for a backend with a smaller entry limit and advised finding and deleting the large KVv2 data. The reporter later confirmed finding and deleting the secret and considered the issue resolved. The later DynamoDB-to-PostgreSQL report in c20 is a different participant and deployment and is deliberately excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the generic `context canceled` result masked a destination `Put` failure; for the resolved Raft path, a 1,742,831-byte KVv2 entry exceeded the 1,048,576-byte destination limit.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: cancellation occurred immediately during the instrumented scan, traversal completed when destination writes were skipped, and direct write logging exposed the Raft size error.

Must not continue treating a slow or oversized GCS prefix as the root cause; the failing prefix contained one object, GCS-client and parallelism changes did not alter the result, and skipping destination writes allowed traversal to complete.

Must explain that migration does not automatically split or repack an entry to fit a destination backend and recommend locating and deleting the oversized KVv2 secret/version when appropriate; changing the destination limit may be discussed as an alternative but was not the reporter's chosen resolution.
Must ask the reporter to rerun the migration after addressing the oversized entry and must not declare resolution until the affected reporter confirms the issue is resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical Vault operator who can build modified Vault binaries, instrument Go code, compare repeated runs, and inspect storage-backend errors, but initially lacks visibility into the migrate command's swallowed write error.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent, investigative, and informal; posts detailed logs and code diffs, corrects earlier assumptions as new evidence appears, and clearly distinguishes the operational workaround from the logging defect.
